price_per_million.source: openrouter.ai/models, confirmed via preflight 2026-11-11; thinking tokens billed as output

research_concepts: play-type possession records derived from play-by-play
methodological_questions: Does adherence to a recommended mix predict game or series wins beyond team quality?
Is the recommendation derived from outcomes it is later tested against (outcome-derived label, leakage)?
Is 54 series enough to detect a plausible adherence effect?
Are play-type labels and suppression estimates reliable at series level?
How should team quality, opponent, and game state confounding be handled?
Do regression to the mean or look-ahead arise when conditioning on suppression?
evidence_establishes: Nothing: retrieval returned no records, so no historical evidence was available for this question.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether this or a similar adherence-predicts-winning question was previously tested, and with what result.
Whether earlier attempts hit leakage, power, or label-reliability problems.
Whether a 'suppression-conditional recommended mix' has a validated definition.
own_inferences: The claim is under-specified: 'recommended mix', 'adherence', 'suppression-conditional', and 'predicts' (game vs series, in-sample vs out-of-sample) are undefined, so as posed it is not yet a falsifiable hypothesis.

If the recommended mix is fitted from outcomes (points per possession or wins) in the same games used to measure adherence, a positive association is nearly guaranteed by construction and would be an artifact.

Teams that win tend to run more efficient play types and get the shots they want, so adherence is likely reverse-caused by game state and team quality (leading teams change play-type mix; garbage time).
54 series gives limited power at series level; game-level units (several hundred games) are clustered within series and give less independent information than their count suggests.
Playoff series are subject to selection: only good teams enter, restricting the range of team quality and strength of the effect.
A credible test needs the recommendation built strictly from prior data (earlier seasons or earlier games in the series) and tested on later games, with team-quality controls.
The most probable results for a naive test are an artifact or an inconclusive result, not a clean supported or rejected.
uncertainties: Operational definition of suppression (opponent play-type efficiency drop vs league average, vs the team's own season baseline) and the minimum possession counts per play type.
Reliability of play-type classification derived from play-by-play, which is not validated here.
Whether the 54 series include 2025-26 playoffs that are only partial on the question date (complete from 2026-06-21), so data version matters.
Number of possessions per play type per team per series, which is likely sparse for rare play types.
Whether the opponent-specific suppression profile is stable enough across games to guide recommendations.

historical_effect.explanation: Retrieval returned an empty list, so the decision rests entirely on the task statement and my own reasoning. No prior findings or failed approaches were available to support or alter it.

blocking_constraints.text: The 'recommended mix' must be defined from data strictly prior to the games it is tested on. If derived from outcomes in the same sample, adherence and winning are mechanically linked.
54 series gives limited power for a modest adherence effect, especially after controlling for team strength, and games are clustered within series.
Team quality, opponent, and game state drive both play-type mix and winning, so adherence is not a clean exposure.

prior_work.summary: No earlier work was retrieved, so whether this question was previously studied is unknown. I rely on none.

risks.text: Best/avoid labels based on efficiency or wins in the evaluation data make adherence predict winning by construction.
Recommendations that use full-series or full-season data, including the games being predicted, leak the future. Use only prior information.
Team quality, home court, opponent strength, and in-game score state (leading teams run different play types) confound adherence and winning.
54 series is small, and game-level analyses are clustered within series.
Few possessions per play type per team per series make mix proportions noisy and the avoid category rarely exercised.
Play-type labels derived from play-by-play and suppression estimates may be noisy and inconsistent across seasons.
Selecting play types as best or avoid on extreme observed suppression or efficiency regresses toward the mean in later games.
Many play types, thresholds, adherence metrics, and outcomes (game, series, margin) invite forking paths.
Better teams win more, so adherence must be compared with a team-strength baseline, not with chance.
Play-type use and defensive schemes shift across seasons and within series, so recommendations built from earlier seasons may not transfer.

design.estimand: Within-matchup, game-level effect of the mix adherence score on win probability and point margin, adjusted for pre-game team strength. Adherence is the similarity of a team's realized play-type mix in a game to a recommendation fixed before that game. The effect of interest is the adjusted log-odds of winning per SD of adherence.
design.unit: Team-game within series (clustered by series) as the primary unit. Series outcome is a secondary descriptive analysis only, given the 54-series count.
design.sample: Pre-register the data version: 2022-23 through 2024-25 regular seasons and playoffs for deriving recommendations (training); a held-out test on 2025-26 playoffs only after it is complete (2026-06-21), plus 2024-25 playoffs by rolling-origin split. State the series count after the cutoff. Exclude garbage-time possessions (a pre-set score margin and clock threshold). Set a minimum possession threshold per play type.
design.power: Before any outcome analysis, run a simulation-based power analysis using the actual clustered structure (about 54 series, with the game count per series) and a plausible effect (for example OR 1.3 per SD of adherence). If power to detect it is below 0.8, label the study exploratory and report effect sizes with intervals only, with no confirmatory claim.
design.controls: Pre-game team strength (prior net rating or Elo from data before the game), home court, opponent strength, rest, and the opponent's suppression profile. Cluster-robust or mixed-effects logistic regression with series random effects. The recommendation is built only from data before each game (rolling or expanding window, or prior seasons), never from the game itself. The adherence metric is pre-specified and uses a score-state-neutral mix, such as first-half or non-garbage possessions only, to limit reverse causation.
design.falsification: (1) Permutation placebo: shuffle recommendations across opponents within the same season and check that adherence to a mismatched recommendation shows no association. (2) Compare against a naive league-average mix baseline, since the suppression-conditional recommendation must add predictive value beyond it. (3) Negative-control outcome such as pre-game rest. (4) Lagged test: adherence in games n and earlier predicting game n+1, not the reverse. A null or placebo-equivalent result means rejected.
design.multiplicity: One primary pre-registered adherence metric and one primary outcome (game win). Margin, series win, and alternative metrics are secondary, with Holm correction across the secondary set. Report all play-type thresholds tried.
design.decision_rule: Support requires all of: (a) the primary adherence coefficient positive with the 95% cluster-robust interval excluding 0 on the held-out data; (b) incremental out-of-sample log-loss improvement over a team-strength-only model; (c) the matched recommendation outperforming the permutation placebo and the league-average baseline; (d) the power check passed. Reject if the interval excludes the pre-set minimum effect of interest and power is adequate. Otherwise report inconclusive. If recommendations cannot be built without outcome information from the test sample, do not proceed.
design.data_version: Freeze the per-game files and graph-database play-type records as of a dated snapshot. Training: 2022-23 to 2024-25. Confirmatory test: 2025-26 playoffs, run only after the complete-data date of 2026-06-21. Record the snapshot hash and the code version before analysis.

methodological_questions: Does adherence to a recommended play-type mix predict game or series wins?
Is the recommendation derived from the same outcomes it is tested against (outcome-derived label, leakage)?
Is 54 series enough power to test adherence effects?
How reliable are play-type labels and suppression estimates at series level?
How to control for team quality and confounding in adherence-winning associations?
Are there regression-to-the-mean or look-ahead issues in conditioning on suppression?
args.query: Adherence to suppression-conditional recommended play-type mix predicts winning; prior studies of best/avoid counter-strategy recommendations against defensive suppression, with series-level testing and failure modes

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-06-16, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
Adhering to a suppression-conditional recommended mix predicts winning.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 54 series

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
